title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Calcul des Ext^i(G_a,G_a)'. The page sets up the computation of the Yoneda Ext groups Ext^i(G_a,G_a) in the category of sheaves of F_p-modules on (Sch/k), k perfect of characteristic p. Ext^i(G_a,G_a) is a right module over End(G_a)=k[F], the twisted polynomial ring in Frobenius.

Proposition: for i>=1 (the inequality is overwritten in the image), Ext^i(G_a,G_a) is F-torsion: every class is killed by some power of F acting on the right.

Corollary, attributed to Milne: let G_a^parf be the restriction of G_a to the perfect site, i.e. the colimit of G_a along F. Then Ext^i(G_a^parf,G_a^parf)=0 for i>=1. The reason is that Ext out of the colimit along F is computed by the limit along F of the F-torsion groups, which vanishes.

Proof strategy:
- For a simplicial sheaf X, use the universal-coefficient spectral sequence E_2^{i,j}=Ext^i_{F_p}(H_j(X),F) => H^{i+j}(X,F), in the category of sheaves of F_p-modules.
- Work 'mod F', a Serre-class (mod C) localisation killing F-torsion modules.
- Known low degrees: Hom(G_a,G_a)=k[F] and Ext^1(G_a,G_a)=0.
- Induction: apply the spectral sequence to X=K(G_a,n) with n large. Here H_j(K(G_a,n))=0 for 0<j<n and H_n=G_a, so the row j=n has E_2^{i,n}=Ext^i(G_a,G_a). The higher homology sheaves are direct sums of copies of G_a, on which p acts as 0.
- H^*(K(G_a,n),G_a) is known from the previous page: a free algebra on admissible Steenrod-type monomials P^I tensored with k[F], with P^0 not equal to 1.
- Comparing the two sides degree by degree (the next page's exact sequence and Lemma 1, 'the edge map ∂ is zero') forces Ext^{i}(G_a,G_a) to be zero modulo F-torsion.

The next page records the answer over F_p: Ext^odd=0 and Ext^{2i}=k[F]/(F^{α}), α=v_p(i) (as written). It also sketches a bar/Koszul spectral sequence computation via suspensions of K(G_a,n) and the dual Steenrod algebra.

This is precisely L. Breen's method and result: 'Extensions du groupe additif', Publ. Math. IHÉS 48 (1978), and the perfect-site version, Breen, 'Extensions du groupe additif sur le site parfait' (c. 1981). Its application to duality is in Milne's Arithmetic Duality Theorems. The page is almost certainly Grothendieck's notes of a lecture (likely Breen's) at the 1976 IHÉS conference.
errors: The inequality in the Proposition is overwritten in the image ('i>1' with a correction, probably to i>=1 or i>0), while the Corollary says i>1. This is harmless since Ext^1(G_a,G_a)=0 in F_p-module sheaves, but it is inconsistent as written.
'H_j(K(G_a,n)) = ⊕ G_a' is schematic. The summands carry Frobenius twists/module structures, and H_0 should be taken as reduced; nothing wrong in substance.

The formula on the next page, Ext^{2i}=k[F]/(F^{v_p(i)}), gives 0 when p does not divide i. That would make many even Ext groups vanish; it should be checked against Breen's precise statement, as the indexing may be garbled in the notes.

Vanishing of Ext^i(G_a,G_a) for i>0 on the perfect site, via colimit along Frobenius
ideas.modern_name: Breen's perfect-site vanishing, used in Milne's flat duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: L. Breen; used by J. Milne (Arithmetic Duality Theorems, Ch. III)
ideas.where_published: Breen, 'Extensions du groupe additif sur le site parfait'; Milne ADT

ideas.what: Universal coefficient spectral sequence for simplicial sheaves applied to K(G_a,n), with stabilisation in n and Steenrod-type operations on H^*(K(G_a,n),G_a)
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–MacLane/stable method for Ext of sheaves (as in Breen, Illusie's Complexe cotangent)

ideas.what: Working modulo the Serre class of F-torsion modules

deep.surprise_reason: These are lecture notes reproducing Breen's well-known computation of Ext(G_a,G_a) and the perfect-site vanishing used by Milne. The material is fully published and properly credited; the page only documents Grothendieck's attendance/notes.
transcription_corrections: 'est de F lorscon' should read 'est de F-torsion'.
The Proposition's inequality is overwritten in the image ('i>1' corrected, probably to 'i≥1').
'fais simpl X' = 'faisceau simplicial X'; 'fais de F_p-modules' = 'faisceaux de F_p-modules'.
'Cor : (Milne)' appears as written; the attribution is to Milne.
